title: ESM: A Framework for Building Effective Surrogate Models for Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search
problem: Hardware-aware NAS relies on surrogate models to efficiently predict performance (latency, energy) of DNN candidates on target devices, but building accurate, reliable prediction models requires systematic understanding of factors influencing prediction quality.
motivation: Efficient DNNs for resource-constrained devices require hardware-aware NAS, but surrogate model inaccuracy limits search quality; understanding model design factors is essential for practical hardware-aware optimization.
method: Systematic analysis of surrogate model types and their strengths/weaknesses for GPU-powered devices. Studies factors influencing prediction accuracy across all pipeline stages (data generation, model selection, training). Presents ESM framework enabling reliable dataset generation and efficient model generation with cost-aware optimization.
key_novelty: Holistic framework for systematic analysis of hardware-aware latency prediction model design, identifying critical factors across the entire surrogate model pipeline for GPU acceleration.
contributions: Systematic analysis of surrogate model types for hardware-aware NAS
Identification of critical factors influencing prediction accuracy
Cost-aware framework for reliable dataset generation
Guidelines for efficient surrogate model generation

metrics.other: Latency prediction accuracy (specific metrics not provided in abstract)

limitations: Evaluation primarily on GPU devices; applicability to other accelerators (TPU, NPU, ASIC) not discussed.
primary_theme: Systematic framework for hardware-aware surrogate models in NAS
